hero.headline: House rejects extension of foreign surveillance law set to expire
hero.body:
The House of Representatives voted 218-198 against extending a powerful surveillance law, ensuring that a controversial foreign intelligence tool will lapse on Friday. The failed vote represents a significant political clash over both national security and personnel decisions within the Trump administration.

Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act, enacted after 9/11, permits U.S. intelligence agencies to intercept communications of foreign targets without obtaining individual court warrants. The law has been credited with stopping terrorist plots, including an alleged scheme targeting a Taylor Swift concert.

Republicans attempted to pass a short-term extension using a fast-track procedure requiring a two-thirds majority. The measure fell short, with 19 Republicans joining most Democrats in opposition. Democrats announced they would block the renewal to protest Trump's appointment of Bill Pulte as acting director of national intelligence.

Pulte, head of the Federal Housing Finance Agency and heir to a home construction company fortune, has faced criticism for lacking relevant national security experience. House Democratic leaders released a statement questioning his qualifications, noting that the position legally requires "extensive" national security experience. They also expressed concern about his willingness to search government databases for information on Trump's political opponents.

"There is a path to reauthorizing FISA, but it will require enacting meaningful reforms," the Democratic statement said. "We oppose this bill to kick the can further down the road."

The congressional impasse comes after a similar failure in the Senate last week, where all Democrats except John Fetterman of Pennsylvania opposed the extension, citing Pulte's appointment. Seven conservative Republicans with civil liberties concerns also voted against the measure.

However, the expiration of Section 702 does not mean surveillance operations will completely halt. The FISA court previously issued a year-long certification allowing collection activities to continue through approximately March 2027, even if the statutory authority lapses. This provision means intelligence agencies can maintain their foreign surveillance operations under the existing court order.

Still, Republican leaders expressed concern about the situation. The chairs of the Senate intelligence and judiciary committees sent a letter to Secretary of State Marco Rubio asking the administration to prepare for a "potential significant gap in foreign intelligence collection."

The debate reflects the ongoing tension between national security advocates who view Section 702 as essential for counterterrorism operations and critics who worry the law enables excessive surveillance of Americans whose communications get incidentally collected when they contact foreign individuals. As the Friday deadline approaches, Congress faces pressure to resolve both the legal authority question and the underlying dispute over Trump's intelligence leadership appointment.

cards.headline: U.S.-Iran deal includes Hormuz reopening and sanctions relief
cards.teaser: The memorandum of understanding calls for immediate reopening of the strait and a 60-day ceasefire extension.
cards.body:
The U.S.-Iran memorandum of understanding President Trump says will soon be signed includes provisions for immediately reopening the Strait of Hormuz without tolls and providing Iran sanctions relief based on compliance. A diplomat from a mediating country and a U.S. official confirmed the terms.

The agreement would extend the current ceasefire for 60 days, including in Lebanon, during which nuclear negotiations would take place. The text includes a framework for addressing Iran's enriched uranium stockpile, though specific actions on the nuclear program remain to be negotiated.

cards.headline: Trump Cancels Next Wave of Strikes on Iran, Says Deal Close
cards.body:
President Trump announced he was canceling planned missile strikes against Iran after claiming the two countries were on the verge of signing a peace agreement. The announcement came after two consecutive days of U.S. military attacks on Iranian targets that threatened to collapse a fragile ceasefire established in April.

Trump made the announcement through social media posts but provided no details about what progress had been made or what terms were being discussed. Iranian leadership quickly disputed his claims, with the foreign ministry saying reports of a deal were "speculative" and that no final decision had been reached.

The timing of Trump's announcement followed escalating military exchanges between the two countries. The U.S. strikes targeted radar and air defense facilities along the Strait of Hormuz in response to the downing of an American Apache helicopter gunship. U.S. officials said the helicopter collided with an Iranian drone, though it remained unclear whether the collision was intentional. The two crew members were rescued in what the military called an unprecedented operation using an unmanned drone boat.

Iran responded to the initial U.S. strikes with its own wave of attacks on Wednesday morning, launching long-range missiles and drones at targets in Kuwait, Bahrain, and Jordan. Iranian officials claimed they struck the U.S. al-Azraq base in Jordan and targeted F-35 fighter jet hangars and command centers. U.S. officials told Reuters that nearly all the missiles and drones were intercepted, with Jordan's armed forces confirming they shot down five missiles before impact.

Trump downplayed the helicopter incident in comments to the Wall Street Journal, calling it "not a big deal" and stating the pilot was fine. He had previously characterized the downing as intentional, blaming Iran and stating the United States could not allow such an action to go unanswered.

U.S. Central Command described the strikes as "a proportional response to unjustified Iranian aggression," signaling the administration was not seeking to escalate toward full-scale war.

Trump had expressed optimism about negotiations earlier in the week, claiming there was "a good chance" of reaching a deal within two or three days. Over the past two months since the April ceasefire, he has repeatedly predicted an agreement was imminent without providing specifics. Vice President JD Vance suggested the conflict could conclude in a week or several months.

Iran's chief negotiator, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, responded to Trump's overtures by stating Iran preferred diplomatic language but spoke "other languages far more fluently," appearing to reference military options.

The conflict has significantly impacted global energy prices and food costs since military operations began in February. Officials have struggled to convert the April ceasefire into a permanent agreement, particularly as Israel continues expanding military operations against the Iranian-backed Hezbollah militia in Lebanon.

cards.headline: Ukraine Strikes Fuel Supplies to Crimea, Sparking Crisis
cards.teaser: Ukrainian attacks on fuel infrastructure have left gas stations in occupied Crimea running dry.
cards.body:
Ukrainian drone strikes targeted fuel supplies to Crimea, creating a fuel shortage across the Russian-held peninsula. Fuel stations in Crimea ran out of gasoline following a fresh night of Ukrainian drone attacks on occupied territories. The strikes intensified an existing fuel crisis in areas under Russian control.

The Russian-installed governor in Sevastopol said fuel trucks failed to reach the city, telling residents that waiting in line at gas stations was pointless. The attacks represent an escalation in Ukraine's strategy of targeting infrastructure in Crimia and other Russian-occupied areas. The fuel shortage affects both civilian and military operations on the peninsula.

cards.headline: Right-Wing Agitation Fuels Violent Riots Across U.K.
cards.teaser: Two stabbings sparked violent protests in England and Northern Ireland, amplified by online right-wing voices.
cards.body:
Two stabbings fueled violent protests in England and Northern Ireland over the last 10 days, fanned online by right-wing voices. The incidents followed a pattern seen across Britain and Europe of hateful attacks leading to right-wing agitation and subsequent riots. The cycle has become increasingly common in the U.K.

Online amplification by right-wing figures has intensified the violence following each incident. The protests have spread across multiple cities in England and into Northern Ireland. The pattern represents a challenge for British authorities trying to prevent violent escalation after individual criminal acts.

cards.headline: Supreme Court blocks Alabama execution by nitrogen gas
cards.teaser: The court prevented Alabama from executing an inmate using nitrogen hypoxia, delaying the execution.
cards.body:
The Supreme Court has prohibited Alabama from executing Jeffrey Lee using nitrogen gas, halting his scheduled execution. Lee remains under a death sentence but will not be executed through the nitrogen hypoxia method the state had planned.

A jury previously voted to sentence Lee to life imprisonment, yet Alabama proceeded with execution plans anyway. The court's decision stops the use of this execution method in Lee's case, though he continues to face capital punishment.

cards.headline: Appeals court allows Trump's 10 percent global tariff to remain
cards.teaser: A federal appeals court ruled the tariff can stay in place while the court considers its final decision.
cards.body:
A federal appeals court ruled Thursday that President Trump's 10 percent global tariff is likely legal and can remain in effect until the court issues a final ruling. Trump imposed the levy after the Supreme Court struck down his previous emergency tariffs as exceeding his authority.

Last month, a federal trade court found the new tariff unlawful and blocked officials from enforcing it against a group of plaintiffs. The appeals court decision reverses that block, allowing the tariff to continue while legal challenges proceed through the court system.

cards.headline: Court Rules South Korean Ex-President Plotted Martial Law
cards.teaser: A court found that impeached former president Yoon Suk Yeol flew drones over North Korea to create instability justifying authoritarian rule.
cards.body:
A South Korean court ruled that former president Yoon Suk Yeol orchestrated drone flights over North Korea as part of a plot to impose martial law in 2024. The impeached leader sought to stir up instability that would justify his bid for authoritarian rule, according to the court's findings.

The drone operations were part of a broader scheme to create a crisis atmosphere. Yoon was impeached and removed from office before he could implement martial law. The court's ruling provides legal confirmation of what prosecutors alleged were deliberate attempts to undermine democratic governance in South Korea.

cards.headline: Toronto Police Officer Killed in Raid Tied to Consulate Shooting
cards.teaser: An officer died during a raid connected to an investigation of gunfire outside the U.S. consulate in March.
cards.body:
A Toronto police officer was killed during an early-morning raid on an apartment in the city's northwest. Constable Marc Pinizzotto, 43, was shot while executing a search warrant and later died in hospital. The raid was linked to an attack on the U.S. consulate that occurred in March.

Police Chief Myron Demkiw confirmed the officer's death. A 19-year-old suspect remains at large and will face charges in connection with the shooting.

cards.headline: U.S. Blocks Florida Company's Fuel Deal with Cuba
cards.teaser: The Trump administration prevented Vanguard Energy from shipping fuel that could have eased Cuba's energy crisis.
cards.body:
The Trump administration blocked a fuel shipment agreement by Florida-based Vanguard Energy to supply Cuba with 250,000 barrels, citing the company's lack of proper authorization. The transaction was halted by federal authorities before it could proceed.

Cuba has struggled with persistent energy shortages that have disrupted electricity generation and affected life across the island. The blocked fuel delivery would have provided relief during the ongoing crisis.

cards.headline: Violent Clashes Erupt Outside World Cup Opening Match
cards.teaser: Police and protesters clashed outside Azteca Stadium as the tournament began in Mexico City.
cards.body:
Mexico's opening match of the 2026 World Cup in Mexico City was marred by clashes between protesters and police outside the stadium. Demonstrators gathered in large numbers to voice their concerns as the tournament began, leading to sporadic violence despite the overall protests remaining largely peaceful.

Inside the venue, Mexico defeated South Africa 2-0, with goals from Julián Quiñones and Raúl Jiménez. The match proceeded with a star-studded opening ceremony. President Claudia Sheinbaum opted to skip the tournament, breaking Mexico's longstanding tradition of presidential attendance at such sporting events.

cards.headline: Kennedy Center board moves to keep Trump name as removal deadline nears
cards.teaser: The Kennedy Center board is fighting a court order requiring removal of the president's name from the venue.
cards.body:
The Kennedy Center board voted Thursday to seek a legal stay of a federal judge's ruling that found Trump's name was illegally added to the performing arts venue. The board has until Friday to comply with the court order to remove the president's name from the facade.

The decision comes as the Trump administration appeals the ruling by US District Judge Christopher Cooper, who determined in May that the name was improperly placed on the federally funded institution.

cards.headline: Major warehouse fire destroys million-square-foot facility in Tracy, California
cards.teaser: A fire destroyed a medical equipment warehouse in Tracy, prompting evacuations at nearby facilities.
cards.body:
A massive fire engulfed a Medline medical equipment warehouse spanning roughly one million square feet in Tracy, California. The fire chief reported that the building's sprinkler system was not working at the time of the blaze.

The city of Tracy declared a local emergency as the fire destroyed the facility. Authorities ordered evacuations at nearby warehouses as firefighters worked to contain the flames.

cards.headline: Trump nominates Jay Clayton as director of national intelligence
cards.teaser: The president selected a U.S. attorney for the top intelligence position after facing criticism over a previous pick.
cards.body:
President Trump nominated Jay Clayton, the former head of the Securities and Exchange Commission, to serve as director of national intelligence. Clayton will oversee the nation's intelligence agencies and serve as the principal intelligence adviser to the president.

The nomination came after Trump faced widespread criticism for his initial decision to install Bill Pulte, a controversial ally, as acting director of national intelligence. The backlash against Pulte's appointment led Trump to pursue a permanent nominee instead.

cards.headline: Tornadoes strike central Illinois as severe storms hit Chicago area
cards.teaser: Two confirmed tornadoes touched down in southwest Illinois as tornado warnings were issued for parts of the region.
cards.body:
Severe storms swept through central Illinois and the Chicago metropolitan area, prompting multiple tornado warnings. Officials confirmed at least two tornadoes touched down in southwest Illinois as the storms moved through the region.

The storms caused power outages affecting utility customers and led to numerous road closures across the Chicago area. Cleanup efforts began in the city and south suburbs as crews worked to restore power and clear debris.

cards.headline: Trump claims Iran settlement reached, Tehran disputes characterization
cards.teaser: The president said a deal to end the Iran conflict has been reached and could be signed this weekend, but Iran says nothing is finalized.
cards.body:
President Trump announced Thursday that a settlement with Iran has been reached and that he is canceling planned missile strikes. He suggested the agreement could be signed as soon as this weekend.

Iran's foreign ministry rejected Trump's characterization, stating that no final decision on an agreement has been made and that reports of a deal are speculative. The announcement followed two days of escalating attacks that threatened to destabilize the existing ceasefire between the two countries.

hero.headline: SpaceX Sets Record IPO Price at $135 Per Share in Largest Public Offering
hero.body:
SpaceX finalized its initial public offering price at $135 per share, creating what will become the largest stock market debut in history. The space exploration, satellite broadband, and artificial intelligence company is selling more than 555 million shares, raising at least $75 billion through the public offering. Trading is set to begin on Friday.

The IPO values SpaceX at approximately $1.78 trillion. At this valuation, founder Elon Musk could become the world's first trillionaire on paper once shares begin trading publicly, though his net worth had declined by more than $50 billion in the period before the offering.

Investor demand for SpaceX shares has been exceptionally strong. Retail investor orders topped $100 billion, while institutional investors like BlackRock placed orders of at least $5 billion. Overall, the offering attracted between $250 billion and $300 billion in bids from investors, meaning it was oversubscribed by three to four times.

The $75 billion raise is nearly three times larger than the previous record IPO. Saudi Aramco's 2019 offering of $29.4 billion held the previous title.

However, not all analysts view the valuation favorably. Morningstar, an investment research firm, has calculated that SpaceX is worth only $63 per share, well below the IPO price. Michael Field, Morningstar's chief equity strategist, stated that the company has "real strengths, particularly in Starlink," but warned of concerns about valuation. "With so many unknown and untested technologies underpinning much of the valuation price, particularly within the AI business, we think the valuation is extremely speculative," Field said. He recommended investors wait for "a more attractive entry point down the line."

Morningstar estimates that Starlink's realistic global market opportunity is around $129 billion, significantly lower than SpaceX's claim of a $1.6 trillion addressable market for the division.

At $1.78 trillion, SpaceX trades at roughly 92 times its trailing sales, an exceptionally high valuation. The company reported a net loss of $4.9 billion in 2025.

U.S. Senator Elizabeth Warren called on the Securities and Exchange Commission to delay the IPO, citing concerns about investor protection and corporate governance given the offering's unprecedented scale.

SpaceX operates three main business segments: space exploration through its Falcon and Starship rockets, connectivity via its Starlink satellite constellation, and artificial intelligence through its xAI division. The company has established itself as a leader in commercial spaceflight while maintaining its satellite network.

Index providers have begun preparing for SpaceX's inclusion in major stock indices. MSCI confirmed it would apply existing rules to include the company in its Global Standard Indexes early. However, S&P Dow Jones Indices declined to relax its entry requirements, meaning SpaceX could take months to join the S&P 500.

cards.headline: Stocks Rally as Trump Signals Progress on Iran Peace Deal
cards.teaser: Markets surged after the president called off additional strikes, saying a deal could be within reach.
cards.body:
President Trump announced he would cancel planned missile strikes on Iran and claimed a peace deal was near. The announcement sparked market gains, with the Dow Jones surging 930 points alongside gains in the Nasdaq and S&P 500. Asian tech stocks also rose following the news.

Oil prices fell and Treasury yields declined as investors reassessed geopolitical risk. Trump made his claims through social media, though Iranian leadership did not immediately confirm any agreement had been reached.

cards.headline: Elon Musk Becomes First Trillionaire on Paper After SpaceX IPO
cards.teaser: The SpaceX public offering pushed Musk's net worth past the trillion-dollar threshold.
cards.body:
Elon Musk has become the world's first trillionaire on paper following SpaceX's initial public offering. The company priced its stock at $135 per share, pushing Musk's net worth past the $1 trillion mark for the first time in history. His wealth spans holdings across SpaceX, Tesla, and other ventures.

The milestone reflects current asset valuations rather than liquid cash reserves. SpaceX's IPO generated significant investor interest, with retail orders exceeding $100 billion and major institutions like BlackRock placing substantial bids. Musk's trillionaire status depends on market valuations that fluctuate based on trading activity and investor sentiment.

cards.headline: Justin Fishner-Wolfson Leads Multibillion-Dollar SpaceX Payout
cards.teaser: A longtime figure in Elon Musk's orbit is managing the distribution of IPO proceeds to shareholders.
cards.body:
Justin Fishner-Wolfson, a SpaceX shareholder who has been a minor figure in Elon Musk's business network, is overseeing a multibillion-dollar payout connected to the company's initial public offering. Fishner-Wolfson's role puts him at the center of distributing proceeds to early investors and employees who hold shares in the rocket company.

The payout structure represents one of the largest distributions of wealth from a single corporate event. Fishner-Wolfson's position managing these transactions gives him significant influence over how and when shareholders receive their returns from the public offering. His involvement highlights the complex financial arrangements behind major IPOs.

cards.headline: World Cup Economics Shape 2026 Tournament Amid Trade Wars
cards.teaser: Trade tensions and soaring ticket prices make this year's World Cup unlike any previous tournament.
cards.body:
The 2026 World Cup is taking place during unprecedented economic turbulence. Trade wars between major economies and dramatically higher ticket prices have fundamentally altered how this tournament operates compared to previous World Cups. These economic pressures are reshaping both the organization of the event and the experience for fans trying to attend.

The tournament offers a window into how global economic shifts affect major international sporting events. Economists are examining what the 2026 World Cup reveals about current international trade dynamics and consumer spending patterns during a period of significant economic change.

cards.headline: India Develops Spirits Industry Using Wild Agave Plants
cards.teaser: Distillers are creating a new category of beverages from agave growing naturally across India.
cards.body:
A spirits industry is emerging in India based on agave plants that grow wild throughout the country. Distillers have begun using the plants to create beverages, establishing what they hope will become a distinct category in the Indian alcohol market. The development represents an effort to build a domestic industry around a naturally occurring resource.

Agave has traditionally been associated with Mexican spirits production, but Indian entrepreneurs are working to establish their own identity and production methods. The wild growth of agave in India provides raw material without the need for extensive cultivation. The new industry could create economic opportunities in regions where the plants are abundant.

cards.headline: Cleve Moler, Computing Interface Pioneer, Dies at 86
cards.teaser: The developer who made complex computing accessible to millions without requiring coding knowledge has died.
cards.body:
Cleve Moler, who built interfaces that allowed engineers, scientists, and everyday users to solve complex problems without writing underlying code, has died at 86. His work made powerful computing tools accessible to people who lacked programming expertise, democratizing access to computational problem-solving across industries.

Moler's contributions to computing centered on creating user-friendly interfaces that abstracted away technical complexity. His software enabled professionals in various fields to perform sophisticated calculations and analysis without needing to master programming languages. The tools he developed became widely adopted in engineering, science, and business applications.

hero.headline: Oracle warns hackers exploited security flaw in mass breach campaign
hero.body:
Oracle issued a security warning about a vulnerability that hackers used to breach more than 100 organizations. The tech giant confirmed the flaw exists in its systems after a cybercrime gang claimed to be exploiting it as part of a widespread hacking campaign. Google notified over 100 organizations that operated potentially vulnerable servers.

The warning comes after evidence emerged that attackers had already used the security bug to compromise corporate networks. Oracle did not specify which product contained the vulnerability or provide technical details about how the exploit works. The company has not disclosed whether a patch is available or when affected customers can expect a fix.

Google's threat intelligence team identified the vulnerable servers and reached out to affected organizations as part of its routine monitoring of security threats. The search giant's involvement suggests the scope of the breach campaign extends across multiple industries and geographies. Organizations running Oracle software now face the task of determining whether their systems are exposed and what data may have been accessed.

Cybercrime gangs increasingly target widely used enterprise software because a single vulnerability can provide access to hundreds or thousands of companies. Oracle's database and cloud products power critical business operations for corporations and government agencies worldwide. A successful exploit of Oracle systems could give attackers access to sensitive financial records, customer data, and internal communications.

The incident highlights ongoing challenges in securing complex enterprise software environments. Organizations that use Oracle products will need to monitor for additional guidance from the company and assess their exposure to the reported vulnerability. Security teams are likely reviewing logs to determine whether their systems show signs of unauthorized access related to this campaign.

cards.headline: SpaceX sets share price at $135 in largest IPO ever
cards.teaser: SpaceX announced its official share pricing as the company begins its initial public offering.
cards.body:
SpaceX confirmed it will price shares at $135 each as it launches what is being called the largest initial public offering in history. The announcement marks the formal start of the company's transition to public trading after years of private ownership.

The share price sets the valuation framework for SpaceX's public debut. The company has not disclosed the total number of shares being offered or the expected proceeds from the IPO.

cards.headline: Jeff Bezos-backed Prometheus raises $12 billion at $41 billion valuation
cards.teaser: Prometheus, a startup developing artificial intelligence for engineering and drug design, completed a funding round valuing the company at $41 billion.
cards.body:
Prometheus, backed by Jeff Bezos, closed a $12 billion funding round at a $41 billion valuation, cementing its position among the most highly valued private AI companies. The physical AI startup is building what it calls an "artificial general engineer" designed for real-world applications.

The company's focus is automating complex tasks in engineering and pharmaceutical research, including drug design processes that traditionally demand significant human expertise. Prometheus aims to develop systems capable of handling heavy engineering work and other specialized domains.

cards.headline: Theker raises $85 million to build reconfigurable factory robots
cards.teaser: Theker secured funding to develop industrial robots designed to be reconfigured for different tasks rather than built around a single fixed form.
cards.body:
Theker raised $85 million to advance its approach to factory automation through robots that can be reconfigured for multiple purposes. Unlike humanoid robots with fixed physical forms, such as those from Boston Dynamics, Theker's machines are designed to be modified for different tasks.

The funding will support development of these adaptable robotic systems for industrial environments. Theker's philosophy emphasizes flexibility, allowing the same robotic platform to handle various manufacturing applications rather than specializing in a single function.

cards.headline: Teardown reveals Trump phone uses existing HTC hardware with Chinese components
cards.teaser: A disassembly of the Trump-branded phone showed the device is nearly identical to an existing HTC model and relies on Chinese-manufactured parts.
cards.body:
Repair specialists conducted a teardown of the Trump phone and discovered it is nearly identical to an existing Taiwanese HTC device. The analysis found the phone contains Chinese-manufactured components, contradicting marketing claims about its manufacturing origin.

The internal hardware and construction closely matched the HTC model with only minimal modifications to differentiate it as a separate product. The findings raised questions about the device's actual origins and the accuracy of its manufacturing claims.

cards.headline: Niantic denies Pokemon Go data shared with drone company
cards.teaser: Niantic responded to reports that environmental scan data from Pokemon Go players was used to develop navigation technology for military drones.
cards.body:
Niantic issued a denial after multiple media outlets reported that spatial data collected through Pokemon Go was being used to train navigation systems for military drones. The reports suggested scans submitted by players, including those in the Netherlands, contributed to drone technology development.

Niantic Spatial, the company's mapping division, disputed claims of data sharing with drone manufacturers. The controversy centers on how player-generated environmental scans are used beyond their stated purpose of improving augmented reality gameplay.

cards.headline: Apple releases iOS 27 Photos app with new features
cards.teaser: Apple introduced updates to its Photos application in iOS 27, including changes to RAW image processing.
cards.body:
Apple released iOS 27 with updates to its Photos app, marking the first significant evolution of its RAW image processing in a decade. The company's camera division discussed how AI tools are being integrated to expand photographic capabilities for users.

The updates include new AI-powered photo editing features and improvements to how the app handles professional image formats. Apple emphasized that the changes give users more control over image processing and editing workflows.

hero.headline: Knicks one win from first NBA title since 1973 after historic comeback against Spurs
hero.body:
The New York Knicks have positioned themselves one victory away from their first championship in 51 years, completing the largest comeback in NBA Finals history to defeat the San Antonio Spurs 107-106 in Game 4.

Facing a 29-point deficit at home, the Knicks mounted an unlikely rally that culminated with OG Anunoby's tip-in with 1.2 seconds remaining. The winning basket came off a missed three-pointer by Jalen Brunson and sent Madison Square Garden into celebration as thousands of fans poured into the streets of Midtown Manhattan.

"Right hand from God," Knicks center Karl-Anthony Towns said of the decisive play.

The Spurs had controlled most of the contest, building a commanding lead early. San Antonio started the game aggressively, forcing Towns to the bench with two fouls before three minutes had elapsed. The Spurs made 11 of their first 16 three-point attempts and led 41-22 after one quarter. By halftime, they held a 76-49 advantage, the largest halftime lead by a visiting team in NBA Finals history.

The turning point arrived in the third quarter. New York limited San Antonio to 14 points on 4-for-20 shooting, with the Spurs struggling particularly in the paint. The Knicks chipped away methodically, entering the final period down just 15 points.

The fourth quarter transformation proved dramatic. The Knicks went on a 28-9 run over seven minutes, converting defensive stops into fast-break opportunities. Brunson delivered the breakthrough with a layup giving New York a 105-104 lead with 1:22 remaining. After the Spurs retook the lead, Brunson's final three-pointer missed, but Anunoby slipped through the defense for the winning tip-in.

The Knicks led for just 53.8 seconds total, but those final 1.2 seconds determined the outcome.

Anunoby finished with 33 points and made 7 of 9 three-pointers, both career playoff highs. Brunson added 36 points and seven assists, while Jose Alvarado contributed 8 points off the bench during the fourth-quarter surge.

Victor Wembanyama led San Antonio with 24 points and 13 rebounds. Dylan Harper added 21 points for the Spurs, who were outscored 58-30 in the second half and made only 3 of 17 three-pointers after halftime.

With the 3-1 series lead, the Knicks can clinch the championship in Game 5 in San Antonio on Saturday night. Only the 2016 Cleveland Cavaliers have overcome a 3-1 Finals deficit to win a championship. The Spurs would need to become just the second team in NBA history to accomplish the feat.

cards.headline: Mexico defeats South Africa 2-0 in World Cup opener at Azteca Stadium
cards.teaser: Mexico opened their World Cup campaign with a victory in front of a home crowd, with Raul Jimenez scoring in his return from a near-fatal injury.
cards.body:
Mexico began the World Cup with a 2-0 victory over South Africa at the packed Azteca Stadium. Julián Quiñones scored early after South Africa's Sphephelo Sithole lost possession just nine minutes into the match. Raúl Jiménez sealed the win, completing a remarkable personal journey after a previous near-fatal incident on the pitch.

The match was dramatic, with three players receiving red cards as the game progressed with strict officiating. The opening was overshadowed by organizational challenges at the stadium, including traffic congestion and poor signage, though Mexican fans remained enthusiastic throughout the contest.

cards.headline: Caitlin Clark scores 32 points in double-double as Fever beat Sky in overtime
cards.teaser: The Indiana Fever defeated the Chicago Sky in overtime behind a dominant performance from their star guard wearing Taylor Swift-branded Nike shoes.
cards.body:
Caitlin Clark recorded 32 points and a double-double as the Indiana Fever survived a comeback attempt by the Chicago Sky to win in overtime. Clark wore Taylor Swift-branded Nike shoes during the game. Sophie Cunningham was out for the matchup, which saw the Sky mount a substantial rally before falling short in the extra period.

The victory highlighted the continued strong pairing of Clark and teammate Aliyah Boston. The duo has formed one of the league's most effective combinations this season, with their chemistry evident in the overtime win. The Fever held off the Sky's comeback attempt to secure the victory.

cards.headline: Shohei Ohtani leaves Dodgers game early with left knee inflammation
cards.teaser: The Dodgers' star exited during their game against the Pirates with knee inflammation, raising concern despite the team securing a series victory.
cards.body:
Shohei Ohtani exited early from the Los Angeles Dodgers' game against the Pittsburgh Pirates with left knee inflammation. The two-way star's early departure came as a concerning development for the Dodgers, though the team managed to win the game and take the series against Pittsburgh.

Ohtani was not the only Dodgers player to leave the game early with an injury. Pitcher Justin Wrobleski also exited due to injury during the same contest. Despite losing both players, the Dodgers completed their series victory over the Pirates.

cards.headline: A.J. Brown connects with Patriots quarterback Drake Maye in early practices
cards.teaser: The newly acquired Patriots receiver has impressed teammates and coaches with his chemistry with the young quarterback during offseason work.
cards.body:
A.J. Brown has made a favorable first impression with the New England Patriots, particularly in his developing connection with quarterback Drake Maye. The receiver's early work with Maye has been described as off to a great start, with highlight catches and on-field communication drawing praise from observers at practice sessions.

Patriots defensive back Jordan Byard commented that Brown will be a nightmare for defenses this season playing alongside Maye. The early chemistry between the quarterback and receiver has continued to impress throughout offseason activities, with multiple reports highlighting their connection during practice sessions.

cards.headline: Texas Attorney General warns Big 12 over potential sanctions against Texas Tech
cards.teaser: Ken Paxton cautioned the conference against taking action related to quarterback Brendan Sorsby following a court order in his favor.
cards.body:
Original Card Text (Unchanged)

Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton warned the Big 12 Conference against sanctioning Texas Tech University in connection with quarterback Brendan Sorsby's case. Sorsby's lawyer separately warned the conference not to circumvent a court order that ruled in the player's favor. Texas Tech officials defended both the school and Sorsby in a video statement.

The case has drawn criticism from some observers who characterize it as a major scandal in college sports enabled by judicial intervention. Texas Tech has indicated it is prepared to pursue legal action if the conference imposes additional sanctions. The dispute involves the intersection of conference rules, state legal authority, and player eligibility.

cards.headline: Three red cards issued in World Cup opening match between Mexico and South Africa
cards.teaser: The tournament opener featured multiple ejections, raising questions about whether officials will maintain strict enforcement throughout the competition.
cards.body:
Referee Wilton Pereira Sampaio issued three red cards during the 2026 World Cup opening match at Mexico City Stadium, ejecting South Africa's Yaya Sithole and Themba Zwane along with Mexico's Cesar Montes. The disciplinary action marked an unusually high number of ejections for a tournament opener.

Mexico defeated South Africa 2-0 in the dramatic opening match played at the packed Azteca Stadium.

hero.headline: Olivia Rodrigo Releases Third Album with New Wave Sound and Split Themes
hero.body:
Olivia Rodrigo released her third studio album, titled "You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love," marking a shift in her musical direction. The album moves away from the pop-punk sound of her previous work toward a new wave style while maintaining her reputation for sharp songwriting and emotional depth.

Produced by Dan Nigro, who has co-written on all three of Rodrigo's albums, the record splits its focus between exploring themes of true love and the angst that defined her earlier releases. Multiple reviews describe the album as one of the year's most engaging releases, with praise directed at Rodrigo's storytelling abilities and visceral emotional expression. The album features a collaboration with Robert Smith, adding to its new wave aesthetic.

Rodrigo has established a pattern of critical success across her three albums. Her debut album "Sour" and sophomore effort "Guts" both received widespread acclaim, and early reviews suggest this third release continues that trajectory. Critics note the album represents a natural evolution in her sound while retaining the core elements that made her previous work resonate with audiences.

The album's release was highly anticipated by fans and the music industry. Rodrigo, now in her mid-twenties, has demonstrated staying power in an industry where many young artists struggle to maintain momentum beyond their initial success. Her partnership with Nigro has proven particularly fruitful, with the producer helping shape her sound across all three records.

The album showcases Rodrigo's ability to balance commercial appeal with artistic growth. By incorporating new wave influences while maintaining her confessional songwriting style, she has avoided the trap of simply repeating her earlier formula. The record's exploration of both romantic fulfillment and emotional turmoil reflects a more nuanced perspective than her earlier work, suggesting her development as both a songwriter and storyteller.

cards.headline: Steven Spielberg's Disclosure Day Opens with $12 Million Globally
cards.teaser: The director's latest film about extraterrestrial contact earned around $12 million in its first day of international release.
cards.body:
Steven Spielberg's new film "Disclosure Day" grossed approximately $12 million globally on its opening day. The film centers on themes involving extraterrestrial contact and explores the intersection between alien arrival and religious belief systems.

Reviews describe the film as drawing on Spielberg's established visual and thematic vocabulary from his previous science fiction work. The movie has generated discussion among faith leaders about how religious institutions would respond to confirmed extraterrestrial life, with the film presenting aliens in opposition to religious frameworks.

cards.headline: Jon Hamm Disqualified from Emmy Guest Actor Race Over Submission Error
cards.teaser: The actor cannot compete for his performance in The Morning Show after the studio made a clerical mistake in his category submission.
cards.body:
Jon Hamm has been disqualified from competing in the Emmy guest drama actor category for his role as Paul Marks in Apple TV's "The Morning Show." The Television Academy ruled him ineligible due to a clerical error during the submission process.

The studio responsible for handling Emmy submissions made the mistake, not Hamm or his representatives. The error prevented his performance from being considered in the guest actor in a drama series category.

cards.headline: Off Campus Production Warns Against Cast Harassment Ahead of Second Season
cards.teaser: The series announced it will remove users from social media who target cast members as it prepares for its upcoming season.
cards.body:
The production team behind "Off Campus" has warned that anyone harassing cast members will be removed from the show's social media accounts. The announcement comes as the series prepares for its second season.

The message addresses ongoing issues with viewers targeting actors appearing in the show. By enforcing these removal policies on social media platforms, the production aims to protect cast members from online abuse during the show's next chapter.

cards.headline: Adults Prequel Episode Set for July Debut on Hulu
cards.teaser: FX will release a standalone episode introducing the friend group before the comedy's second season arrives in August.
cards.body:
FX announced a prequel episode for the ensemble comedy "Adults" will debut on Hulu on July 31. The standalone installment introduces the central friend group and reveals the origin story of Paul Bakers, played by Jack Innanen, ahead of the show's second season launch in August.

The network screened the episode as a surprise at the Tribeca Festival. The prequel approach offers viewers background on the show's characters before the new season begins, providing context for relationships and dynamics that will continue in the upcoming episodes.

cards.headline: Emerson, Lake and Palmer Song Adapted into Dystopian Film
cards.teaser: The progressive rock band's epic "Karn Evil 9" is being developed into a science fiction movie with director Isaac Ezban attached.
cards.body:
A film adaptation of Emerson, Lake and Palmer's "Karn Evil 9" is in development as a dystopian science fiction project. Isaac Ezban, the director of "The Incident" and "Párvulos," will helm the film, with Tim Hedrick providing the screenplay.

The ambitious project draws inspiration from the band's epic progressive rock anthem, originally released on the 1973 album "Brain Salad Surgery." This marks an unusual collaboration between classic rock music and contemporary science fiction filmmaking.

cards.headline: Barcelona Grand Prix Streaming Guide Released for F1 Fans
cards.teaser: Viewing options are available for the upcoming race following Andrea Kimi Antonelli's fifth win of the season in Monaco.
cards.body:
Online streaming information has been released for the Barcelona-Catalunya Grand Prix as Formula 1 continues its 2026 season. The race follows the Monaco Grand Prix, where Mercedes driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli secured his fifth victory of the season after 78 laps, earning 156 points.

Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton finished second in Monaco, with Red Bull Racing's Isack Hadjar taking third place. Antonelli leads the championship standings seven rounds into the season. The Barcelona race represents the next opportunity for drivers to challenge his dominance in the current campaign.

hero.headline: Kennedy Center board appeals order to remove Trump's name from building
hero.teaser: The board of trustees voted to appeal a federal judge's order requiring removal of the president's name from the performing arts center.
hero.body:
The Kennedy Center's board of trustees appealed a federal judge's order requiring the removal of President Trump's name from the performing arts venue, filing court documents Thursday just before the judge's deadline. The board also voted to seek a stay of the ruling, according to a person familiar with the private meeting.

U.S. District Judge Christopher Cooper issued his decision on May 29, finding that Trump's name was illegally added to the building. The judge sided with a lawsuit brought by Rep. Jamie Raskin and other plaintiffs seeking removal of the signage from the Washington facility.

Cooper's 94-page ruling determined that the Kennedy Center's founding statute requires the venue to be named for President John F. Kennedy and prohibits other formal names or public memorials without congressional action. "Congress gave the Kennedy Center its name, and only Congress can change it," Cooper wrote.

The building's exterior still displayed "The Donald J Trump and The John F Kennedy Memorial Center for the Performing Arts" as of Monday afternoon, though the Kennedy Center had begun removing Trump's name from its website. The center's general counsel issued a memo instructing employees to change email signatures, letterheads, and other documents to refer to the venue simply as "The John F Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts" or "Kennedy Center." The deadline for completing changes to templates, forms, signage, brochures, and website pages was set for June 12, 2026.

The appeal could extend the legal dispute over Trump's name on the building, with no timeline established for resolution.

Cooper also temporarily blocked the Kennedy Center from closing for renovations this summer. The board, composed of Trump's appointees, had approved a $257 million "revitalization project" that would have shuttered the center for two years. The judge halted this plan as part of his ruling.

Trump responded to Cooper's decision with a lengthy statement on social media, expressing his lack of interest in pursuing what he characterized as a "hopeless journey."

The dispute reflects broader tensions surrounding Trump's second term and his influence on institutions where his name was added during his presidency. The Kennedy Center case represents one of the legal challenges now confronting decisions made by his appointed board members. The outcome will likely depend on the appeals court's interpretation of the center's statutory requirements and whether Congress might need to take action to formally resolve the naming dispute.

cards.headline: Appeals court allows Trump's 10 percent global tariff to remain
cards.teaser: A federal appeals court ruled the tariff can stay in place while the court considers its final decision.
cards.body:
A federal appeals court ruled Thursday that President Trump's 10 percent global tariff is likely legal and can remain in effect until the court issues a final ruling. Trump imposed the levy after the Supreme Court struck down his previous emergency tariffs as exceeding his authority.

Last month, a federal trade court found the new tariff unlawful and blocked officials from enforcing it against a group of plaintiffs. The appeals court decision reverses that block, allowing the tariff to continue while legal challenges proceed through the court system.

cards.headline: Trump pulls back from Iran strike after regional leaders intervene
cards.teaser: President Trump reversed a threat to strike Iran after receiving calls from senior officials in Qatar, the United Arab Emirates, and Pakistan, who assured him a.
cards.body:
President Trump announced he would cancel planned missile strikes against Iran after receiving calls from senior officials in Qatar, the United Arab Emirates, and Pakistan. The regional leaders assured Trump that a diplomatic agreement was within reach, prompting him to allow negotiations to continue.

Trump claimed a "great settlement" with Iran is near and stated he is ready to sign a memorandum of understanding. The proposed agreement would reopen the Strait of Hormuz without tolls and provide Iran with sanctions relief based on its compliance. Iran has disputed reports of a finalized deal, describing them as speculative.

cards.headline: Sen. Cornyn predicts Trump will face difficult two years after midterms
cards.teaser: The Texas senator said in an interview the period following November elections will be challenging for the president.
cards.body:
Sen. John Cornyn of Texas predicted that the two years following the November midterm elections will be the most miserable of President Trump's life, according to a new interview. Cornyn made the remarks to The New York Times in his first extensive interview since losing his primary race to Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, whom Trump had endorsed shortly before the election.

Cornyn's prediction suggests he expects significant political challenges ahead for the president in the post-midterm period, though he did not elaborate on the specific factors that would contribute to those difficulties.

cards.headline: Former Biden ambassador considered presidential run over border policy
cards.teaser: Ken Salazar writes in his upcoming memoir he contemplated a 2024 campaign due to frustration with border management.
cards.body:
Former U.S. Ambassador to Mexico Ken Salazar explored the idea of running for president in 2024, driven by disagreements with how the Biden administration managed the southern border. He discusses this consideration in his upcoming memoir, "Borderlands: My Fight for an Inclusive America."

Salazar ultimately decided against entering the race. His book examines his tenure as ambassador and his perspective on U.S.-Mexico relations during the Biden years.

cards.headline: Disability groups sue to block New York medical aid in dying law
cards.teaser: Organizations filed a federal lawsuit arguing the law pushes vulnerable residents toward suicide instead of providing support.
cards.body:
Disability rights organizations filed a federal lawsuit in New York seeking to block the state's Medical Aid in Dying law. The lawsuit argues the law illegally pushes vulnerable New Yorkers toward suicide rather than providing them with support and medical care.

The legal challenge comes as New York joins other states that have enacted legislation allowing terminally ill patients to request medication to end their lives. The plaintiffs contend the law fails to protect disabled individuals from coercion.

cards.headline: Senate Minority Leader Schumer says Democrats positioned for gains
cards.teaser: The New York senator told reporters his party has laid groundwork for a political resurgence despite his unpopularity with the base.
cards.body:
Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer said the political fortunes of Senate Democrats have improved and credited deliberate preparation for the shift. Schumer acknowledged he is not popular with the base of his own party but maintained he has positioned Democrats for gains.

Schumer told reporters his work has laid the groundwork for a Democratic resurgence in upcoming elections. The New York senator has faced criticism from progressive Democrats but said strategic decisions during his time as minority leader will benefit the party.
